title: Generalized Wasserstein Flow Matching: Nested Couplings for Point Cloud Generation
claim: Only the nested coupling using Wasserstein plans at both levels produces straight transport paths; weaker couplings give curved, bent trajectories.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, coupling labels as math captions, four colored groups each
description: Three boxed panels sit side by side, captioned (a) (OP_ind, IP_ind), (b) (OP_ind, IP_W) and (c) (OP_W, IP_W). Each panel shows four colour-coded groups (blue, orange, green, red) for the offsets h. Within a group, small circles at the bottom are the source point clouds. Larger offset circles at the top are the targets, shown as triangles and dots. Thin translucent curves link source to target points to show the learned flow paths. In panels (a) and (b) the paths bow into pronounced curved or hooked shapes, and (a) is the most tangled. In panel (c) the paths are nearly straight vertical lines. The eye goes first to the contrast between the curved bundles on the left and the straight ones on the right. The mathematical captions identify the outer and inner coupling choices.
caption: \revise{Learned paths from source circles (bottom) to larger, offset targets (top), $h\in\{-20,-10,10,20\}$ by colour. Only the WoW coupling yields straight paths.}
abstract: We formulate flow matching on probability measures over probability measures. Directly from the Wasserstein-on-Wasserstein (WoW) continuity equation, we show that admissible nested outer and inner couplings induce a valid metameasure flow and non-local velocity field. Validity requires neither optimal plans nor a smooth manifold. Practically, this opens up the design space of multisample flow matching: exact Wasserstein plans are distinguished by energy and straightness, while sliced and lazy linear plans yield scalable alternatives. Point-cloud experiments, including controlled Bures-Wasserstein and Euclidean minibatch baselines, demonstrate the resulting geometry-cost trade-off.
